Rates are per Earth day and per crew member unless the key says otherwise. The rules clock counts Earth hours in a sol of 24 h 39 min (hour 0 to 24.66), not the look clock's 24 local hours.

body.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: the commander's own needs (`body`) wait until Sol 1 has taught them (choice body_on)

body._note: The commander's own needs, shown as Crew health. Game rules: a real body lasts days where the game's lasts hours, because a sol is 20 minutes of play and a kid must feel a need within one. They tick only with knob `body` on and never while the crew sleeps. Hours are awake game hours (1 is about 49 s of play)

health.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: the meter runs 0 to 100; at 0 the mission is lost

water_h.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: a full drink lasts 8 awake hours, so two drinks a sol. Real: 2 kg of drink a day and sweat is water (rows 25, 123), which is why hurrying (effort) empties it faster

food_h.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: a meal lasts 12 awake hours, so breakfast and dinner

rest_h.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: 20 hours awake before tiredness costs health. Real: at least 8.5 h of sleep a sol (row 188), which leaves about 16 awake

suit_pace.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: the suit's 8 h (row 135) run down at half the clock's pace. The hero walks at real speed (1 m/s) while a sol passes in 20 minutes of play, so at the clock's pace the walk to the reactor and back (170 m each way, Sol 2) emptied a full suit (15 Nov, the story test's bot: suit air 0). At half, a full suit is about 13 minutes of walking or 5 of hurrying: the reactor on foot costs under half

effort_hurry.factcheck: row 254 (a forced walk-back used 0.4 lb of oxygen an hour against Apollo's usual 0.15: 2.67 times), row 255 (suited walkers were limited by cooling). The root sets it as `effort` while the hero hurries on foot; suit air and body water drain by it

hurt_per_h.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: health points a game hour while a need is unmet. thirst: an empty water gauge loses the mission in 6.25 game hours (about 5 minutes of play), an empty food gauge in 12.5, so a sol without a drink is a lost mission (15 Nov playtest: at 8 and 4 nobody noticed). air: outside with the suit's air gone (row 135: a suit holds 8 h), 0 in 40 game minutes; cold: the battery at 0, so the heat is off

weak_health.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: Crew health under which the commander weakens (sim.weak, 0 to 1 at health 0): the hero stops hurrying and walks slower. An empty water, food or rest gauge is 1 at once

hurt_per_msv.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: health per mSv of a flare's dose, so the X12 day unsheltered (row 37, 8.1 mSv) costs about 32 and the water shelter halves it (row 90). The real dose was 30 chest X-rays, not deadly: never tell a kid it was

dust_per_h_tau.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: suit dust gathered an hour outside per unit of sky opacity over clear (power.tau_clear), so only in a dusty sky

dusty.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: suit dust at which coming inside unbrushed counts (the HUD's dust mark)

dust_grace_h.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: about 12 s of play inside to brush the suit before the dust is in the cabin

hurt_dust.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: health lost once when a dusty suit comes inside. Real: Mars dust holds 0.5 to 1% perchlorate and is 'likely toxic' (row 140); suitports keep it out of the cabin (row 142)

heal_sleep.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: health a night's sleep gives back (row 188: 8.5 h of sleep)

sleep_water.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: share of body water a night uses, so the morning starts with a drink

sleep_food.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: share of body food a night uses, so the morning starts with breakfast

heal_salad.factcheck: game rule, not a fact: health a fresh salad gives. Real: a 15 g salad gives 8% of a day's vitamin C (row 121), and lettuce takes 33 days (row 29)

labels._note: the cause-log line for each kind of harm (top_causes): one a sol
labels.cold: The battery ran out: the base went cold

harvest_food_kg.factcheck: row 121 (a 15 g salad, one each for 2 crew)

harm_scale._note: how top_causes() weighs meters against each other, game weights, not facts: a cause's share of the whole stay's stock (o2, water, food), of full health (body.health), and of the energy the base makes over the stay (reactor 10 kW x 24.66 h + 190.8 kWh of clear sun, x 30.85 sols, our maths). Energy was weighed against the battery, and a lamp the reactor paid for outranked the thirst that lost the mission. A flare's dose is no longer weighed: its cost is health (body.hurt_per_msv)

body_on.label: Your body needs air, water, food and sleep

uses._note: use spots. `set` fills one of the body's needs (body). The base's stocks do not pay for a drink or a meal: the daily rates already count them (counting them twice would lie). `plant` changes nothing in the rules: the bed regrows after each harvest (row 29: cut-and-come-again), and resetting its age wiped the lettuce the robots planted

o2_leak.label: Oxygen leak
o2_leak.factcheck: a story event with no `source`, so it is not in state().events (the HUD tags those ARCHIVED data); state().leak tells of it. game rule, not a fact: 5 kg an hour, so the tank visibly drops and is empty in about 9 game hours; it runs until the valve is closed (use o2_valve), and what leaked is gone

schedule._note: when events happen: the story's. Sol 5's flare comes half an hour after the 06:30 wake, so the kid has the morning's hour to reach the shelter (row 35). Sol 2's night gust dusts the wings, so the morning's power is lower and a brush lifts it (data/sols.json Sol 2). The dust storm starts in the night of Sol 9, after the rover trip, so the kid wakes into it on Sol 10, Mission 1's finale, with the sky already at its darkest (design/plans/mission-1.md; rise_h 10)
